LESSON: WESTERN STYLE SOLO SONGS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Performing
Topic 2.2: Western Style Solo Songs
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 11

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Western Style Solo Songs, part of Performing in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How should one prepare to perform a Western solo song 2. Why are vocal techniques important in Western solo songs?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to or watch live or recorded performances of lieder, arias from operas and oratorios, and solo songs from musicals for familiarization. Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view. Screen resolution and light intensity could be regulated for learners who are sensitive to light (Apply this adaptation in the subsequent learning experiences involving watching), 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to or watch live or recorded performances of lieder, arias from operas and oratorios, and solo songs from musicals for familiarization. Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view. Screen resolution and light intensity could be regulated for learners who are sensitive to light (Apply this adaptation in the subsequent learning experiences involving watching), 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Western Style Solo Songs together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: The learner confidently performs arias and western solo songs before an audience using the techniques

learnt.

• Citizenship: The learner performs western solo songs gaining knowledge on other global cultures.

• Learning to learn: The learner identifies challenges in executing performance styles in western solo songs and seeks

clarification of how to perform them.

• Digital literacy: The learner utilises digital devices to source for and record performances of Western solo songs.

Values:
• Respect: The learner appreciates others’ views when giving and receiving feedback on their performances.

• Integrity: The learner acknowledges the source of pieces of music sourced from online platforms and from other

musicians for performance.

• Responsibility: The learner uses digital devices for the intended purposes.

• Social justice: The learner gives objective views on peers’ performances.

• Peace: The learner works in harmony with others as they rehearse, perform and critique others’ performances.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Healthy Relationships: The learner collaborates with others in group work as they discuss, rehearse, perform and

critique their performances.

• Life skills: The learner grows their music talent by learning styles and techniques of rehearsal and performance.

• Cyber Security: The learner uses digital apps responsibly as they source and record music.

Suggested Learning Resources

Sheet music, Portfolios, Anecdotal records, Song books, ICT devices, Internet connectivity, Props and costumes
